Title: Camera traps installed in Fraser's Hill to track tiger spotted there
Article:
KUANTAN: The Pahang Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan) has installed four camera traps after receiving reports of a Malayan tiger roaming by the roadside along the Fraser's Hill route near Raub.
Pahang Perhilitan director Yusoff Shariff said his department received information regarding the incident about 9am yesterday.
"Four Perhilitan officers went to the location to conduct an investigation and install camera traps," he said when contacted.
He added that monitoring in the area will continue to gather further information regarding the presence of the tiger.
It was
reported
that several photographs depicting the animal's presence went viral on social media, sparking various reactions from the public.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget described as 'SME Budget'
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Small and Medium Enterprises Association of Malaysia (Samenta) has described the 2027 Budget as an "SME Budget".
It also endorsed the declaration of 2027 as "Malaysia MSME Year" by Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Minister Steven Sim Chee Keong.
Samenta president Datuk William Ng said the budget placed micro, small and medium enterprises at the forefront of the nation's economic momentum.
He said the financing package and tax cut would provide direct cash flow relief and help businesses address core operating overheads.
He said the government's decision to exempt SMEs from the revised RM2,000 minimum wage proves that the 2027 Budget was formulated around the operational realities of small business owners.
The exemption applies to micro, small and medium enterprises with annual sales below RM50 million.
Ng also endorsed the Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Ministry's ABCD Framework, which he said offered a targeted roadmap to scale the "missing middle".
He said the framework would enable local small businesses to modernise, integrate into high-value supply chains and compete regionally.
Describing itself as the country's oldest and largest SME association, Samenta said it would work closely with the minister and the ministry on ground-level implementation.
"The immediate priority is to ensure these budgetary initiatives, particularly financing facilities, digital automation support, and export market access, are disbursed rapidly with minimal red-tape so that the full benefits of this 'SME Budget' are felt across our business community," Ng said in a statement.
One of the
key announcements
under the 2027 Budget is that total loan facilities and financing guarantees will increase from RM50 billion to RM57 billion next year, while income tax rates for micro, small and medium enterprises will be cut by one percentage point.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim also announced that the
minimum wage
would be raised from RM1,700 to RM2,000 a month from June 2027, benefiting more than four million workers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: KL Car Free Morning cancelled due to haze
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Kuala Lumpur Car Free Morning (KLCFM) programme, scheduled to take place at Dataran DBKL here tomorrow, has been cancelled due to the haze.
The KLCFM Working Committee said the decision was made after taking into account the risks participants could face from haze exposure, particularly while engaging in outdoor physical activities.
"The event scheduled for Sunday, Oct 11, at Dataran DBKL has been cancelled.
"The safety, health and well-being of all participants have always been the organisers' priority," it said in a statement.
The organisers also apologised for any inconvenience caused and expressed their appreciation for the public's support and understanding.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kedah schools to operate as usual tomorrow despite haze
Article:
ALOR SETAR: All educational institutions in Kedah will operate as usual tomorrow as the Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at all monitoring areas in the state were recorded below 100 as of 2pm today.
The Kedah State Education Department (JPN) said in a statement that this is, however, subject to further directives from the Education Ministry and relevant authorities.
"The Kedah JPN expresses its appreciation for the concern and decree of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, regarding the importance of safeguarding the safety, health and welfare of students and education personnel following the haze affecting several areas in the country.
"The API readings are below 100, so all educational institutions in Kedah will operate as usual," the statement said.
The Kedah JPN said school administrators and educational institutions had nevertheless been reminded to remain alert to the latest developments, monitor API readings through official Department of Environment channels and take appropriate measures to ensure the safety and health of students and education personnel.
"Schools should also pay close attention to students and education personnel experiencing health problems, particularly those who are sensitive to air quality conditions, and take appropriate action if any students or education personnel show signs of ill health.
"The Kedah JPN will continue to monitor developments in the haze situation and coordinate action with all District Education Offices and educational institutions based on the latest readings and directives from the authorities," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget: Hospital outsourcing scheme to cover more patients, specialities
Article:
IPOH: The Health Ministry will expand its Hospital Services Outsourcing Programme (HSOP) to cover more patients and potentially new specialities following an increase in its allocation to RM200 million under the 2027 Budget.
Its deputy director-general of health (medical), Datuk Dr Mohd Azman Yaacob, said the additional RM56 million would enable the ministry to refer more patients to private hospitals for treatment.
He said the ministry was also studying the possibility of extending the programme to other specialities, including oncology.
"HSOP aims to reduce waiting times and ease congestion at government hospitals.
"We will increase the number of patients who can receive treatment at private hospitals and explore expanding the programme to other specialities," he said.
Dr Azman was speaking to reporters after attending a public-private partnership initiative involving cataract surgery at Perak Community Specialist Hospital (PCSH) here today.
Also present were Perak Chinese Maternity Association secretary-general Datuk Lim Si Boon and Perak Health Department director Datuk Dr Feisul Idzwan Mustapha.
Yesterday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced under the 2027 Budget that RM200 million would be allocated to outsource patients' treatment to other hospitals to reduce waiting times, particularly at urban hospitals.
Introduced in 2024, HSOP currently covers nephrology, cardiology, cardiothoracic surgery, paediatric cardiology and radiology.
Under the programme, patients requiring medical imaging services, including ultrasound scans, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and computed tomography (CT) scans, can be referred to participating private healthcare facilities.
The programme also covers selected cardiac procedures, including angiograms and coronary artery bypass surgery.
Dr Azman said the initiative was particularly important in reducing waiting times for medical imaging services, with patients at government hospitals sometimes having to wait between three and six months for CT scans.
He said private hospitals participating in the programme had to agree to the rates offered before accepting referrals from government hospitals.
"Patients will receive the required treatment and follow-up care at private facilities before returning to their referring government hospitals to continue their treatment," he said.
He added that HSOP did not mean patients would receive treatment entirely free of charge.
"Patients will continue to pay the applicable charges imposed at government hospitals, while the government will cover the remaining treatment costs through the programme.
"For example, if the actual cost of treatment at a private hospital is RM3,000, patients would pay the applicable government hospital charges, while the government would cover the balance through HSOP," he said.
On the cataract surgery initiative, Dr Azman said between 1,500 and 2,000 patients were awaiting surgery at Hospital Raja Permaisuri Bainun here.
He said the ministry would continue to explore partnerships with private healthcare providers beyond the Klang Valley to help patients nationwide receive treatment sooner.
"With initiatives such as this, we can ensure these procedures are carried out earlier, allowing patients to receive treatment more promptly.
"We will continue to explore opportunities to work with private hospitals and specialist centres, including PCSH, to sustain these initiatives.
"We have already established similar collaborations with other parties in the Klang Valley. However, these efforts should not be confined to the Klang Valley, as many more Malaysians need timely surgery to improve their quality of life," he said.
Meanwhile, Lim said the collaboration with PCSH involved 40 cataract operations costing about RM250,000, with the expenses borne by the hospital.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: El-Sisi invites Sultan Ibrahim, Anwar to visit Egypt
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi has extended an invitation to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to visit Egypt.
The president, who is on a two-day state visit to Malaysia, also thanked Sultan Ibrahim for conferring the Darjah Utama Seri Mahkota Negara (DMN) on him at Istana Negara earlier today.
"It speaks much to the depth and strength of the relations between our two countries," he said at a joint press conference with Anwar at the Seri Perdana Complex, Putrajaya today.
El-Sisi also touched on cooperation with Malaysia in key areas including energy and renewable energy, manufacturing, electronics, agriculture, and food industries.
He said both countries were seeking to translate their strong bilateral relations into tangible outcomes, with energy, manufacturing, electronics, agriculture, and food industries identified as key areas for expanded cooperation.
The president added that the potential for collaboration was significant, provided both countries combined their capabilities with strong political will and commitment.
"I believe that the understanding, the mutual trust, and the reciprocal political will of both parties shall enhance our cooperation and take our relationship to a whole new level," he said.
In a joint statement today, Anwar and El-Sisi announced the elevation of bilateral relations between Malaysia and Egypt to a Strategic Partnership.
"Under this framework, both leaders reaffirmed their shared interest in accelerating efforts in building a more dynamic and resilient partnership across all sectors, thereby jointly promoting global prosperity and stability.
"Both leaders acknowledged the importance of regular dialogue through existing bilateral institutional mechanisms and in this regard, agreed to convene the second Joint Commission Meeting (JCM) and the second Bilateral Consultations (BC) at the earliest opportunity," the statement read.
Meanwhile, El-Sisi said he and Anwar also discussed al-Azhar University's instrumental role in the teaching and practice of moderate Islam.
"Egypt is receiving students, males and females, from all over the world, especially from Malaysia, which we are really proud of. They are very bright young men and women, and we are proud of them and proud of everybody who comes to seek education and knowledge in Egypt.
"We are not only ready to increase the number of Malaysian students, but also to exchange scholars and preachers, so that they can disseminate moderation and tolerance of Islam in this beautiful country," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teenager drowns at Kuantan beach
Article:
KUANTAN: A trip to the beach turned tragic when a 16-year-old boy drowned at Pantai Sepat along Jalan Kuantan-Pekan here today.
Pahang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director Mohd Salahuddin Isa said the body Mohamad Raiyan Khairul Anuar was found about 50m from where he was last seen in the water.
"The department received a report of the incident at 9.56am, and despatched six firemen from the Kuantan station.
"Four divers from the department's Water Rescue Unit in Kuantan and Pekan were later deployed to assist in the search. The victim was subsequently found and pronounced dead at the scene by medical personnel," he said in a statement.
Salahuddin said the victim's remains were handed over to police for further action.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze: 28 areas nationwide record unhealthy air quality at 5pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Johor and Selangor remained among the states most affected by the haze, with 28 areas nationwide recording unhealthy air quality as of 5pm today.
According to the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), eight air quality monitoring stations in Johor recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, followed by four in Selangor.
In Johor, Tangkak recorded the highest API reading at 185, followed by Larkin and Pasir Gudang (182), Segamat and Batu Pahat (176), Kluang (173), Kota Tinggi (171) and Pengerang (170).
In Selangor, Shah Alam recorded an API reading of 159, followed by Johan Setia (157), Petaling Jaya (155) and Klang (147).
The other 16 monitoring stations recording unhealthy API readings were located in Negri Sembilan, Pahang, Perak, Kuala Lumpur, Melaka, Putrajaya and Sarawak.
In Kuala Lumpur, Cheras recorded an API reading of 169, while Batu Muda recorded 160. Putrajaya recorded 161. In Negri Sembilan, Seremban recorded an API reading of 172, followed by Nilai (168) and Port Dickson (160).
In Pahang, Rompin recorded 170, followed by Balok Baru in Kuantan (153) and Indera Mahkota (152). In Perak, Tasek in Ipoh recorded an API reading of 169, followed by Pegoh in Ipoh (166) and Tanjung Malim (165).
In Melaka, Alor Gajah, Bukit Rambai and Melaka Town each recorded an API reading of 165, while Kuching in Sarawak recorded 153.
Meanwhile, 40 other air quality monitoring stations nationwide recorded moderate API readings, according to APIMS data. No areas recorded good air quality.
API readings of 0 to 50 are classified as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, and readings above 300 as hazardous.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: El-Sisi departs after 2-day state visit to Malaysia
Article:
SEPANG: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi departed Malaysia today after concluding his two-day state visit at the invitation of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia.
The special aircraft carrying El-Sisi took off from the Bunga Raya Complex (BRC) at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) at 4.38pm.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin were present to bid farewell to the Egyptian leader.
Earlier, El-Sisi inspected a guard of honour mounted by officers and personnel from the First Battalion of the Royal Ranger Regiment, led by Captain Muhammad Nafis Norshid.
A cultural performance by the Istana Budaya arts troupe was also held to mark his departure, showcasing Malaysia's rich cultural heritage through traditional dances and musical performances featuring traditional instruments.
The visit was El-Sisi's first to Malaysia since he assumed office in June 2014.
During the visit, El-Sisi was accorded a state welcoming ceremony at Istana Negara, where Sultan Ibrahim granted an audience to the Egyptian president and his delegation. The King also witnessed a presentation of royal tokens of appreciation at Dewan Seri Maharaja.
Sultan Ibrahim subsequently hosted a state banquet at the Grand Banquet Hall in honour of El-Sisi and the Egyptian government delegation.
El-Sisi and Anwar then held a four-eyed meeting at the Seri Perdana Complex, marking a significant step towards elevating Malaysia-Egypt relations to a strategic partnership after more than six decades of diplomatic ties.
The meeting provided an opportunity for both leaders to review bilateral cooperation, explore new areas of collaboration and exchange views on regional and international developments of mutual interest.
The two countries also exchanged four memoranda of understanding (MoUs) covering women's empowerment, higher education, tourism and investment. The exchange was witnessed by Anwar and El-Sisi.
Anwar also expressed his appreciation to El-Sisi for personally facilitating Malaysia's humanitarian assistance to Palestinians, including efforts to bring injured victims from Gaza to Malaysia for medical treatment.
The prime minister said Egypt had provided significant support for Malaysia's humanitarian initiatives, with coordination facilitated directly through the Egyptian president's office and the country's military intelligence.
In 2025, Egypt was Malaysia's seventh-largest trading partner in Africa, with total bilateral trade valued at RM3.08 billion (US$720 million).
Malaysia's exports to Egypt amounted to RM2.55 billion (US$600 million), while imports totalled RM530 million (US$120 million).
From January to August 2026, bilateral trade rose 74.7 per cent to RM3.49 billion (US$870 million).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Black river waters, dead fish leave Raub villagers worried
Article:
RAUB: Frustration is mounting among villagers in Kampung Sungai Pasu after Sungai Gali, a popular fishing spot, turned black and began emitting a foul smell.
Various species of dead fish have been spotted floating downstream, raising fears of serious water pollution.
Sungai Pasu village headman Mohd Zaidi Hashim said the river, which is usually brownish, turned black several days ago, with dead fish floating on the surface.
"Something is not right with the water... a farmer upstream noticed that the water had turned black on Wednesday but did not suspect anything until various fish species were found dead yesterday.
"Sungai Gali is a popular spot for villagers to fish and cast their nets, but the strong stench has kept them away. The dead fish include baung (catfish) and tilan (spiny eels)... even tilan known for its ability to survive in poor water conditions have been found dead," he told the
New Straits Times
today.
Zaidi said the pollution was believed to have entered Sungai Lampan before spreading downstream to other rivers along the waterway, including Sungai Gali.
"We are worried that the dark colour could be caused by toxic waste, which might affect the livelihoods of villagers who depend on fish caught in the river. So far, the discoloured water has reached rivers in Kampung Kuala Gali and Pia.
"Everyone is concerned because this is the first time the water has changed colour," he said, adding that the Department of Environment (DoE) had collected water samples yesterday.
Earlier, Dong assemblyman Datuk Fadzli Mohamad Kamal said Sungai Gali and Sungai Lampan had been
severely polluted
, threatening river ecosystems and disrupting villagers' daily lives.
He called for immediate action to prevent further damage to the rivers and stop the pollution from spreading to other waterways.
Meanwhile, villager Ahmad Abdullah, 40, said residents usually cast their nets below the bridge in Kampung Sungai Pasu, where fish were abundant, including some exceptionally large baung.
"The polluted river and dead fish have kept anglers away. I do not think anyone will return to cast their nets until the authorities confirm the source of the pollution," he said.
Pahang DoE director Zakaria Ahmad said water samples had been collected and were awaiting analysis by the Chemistry Department.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Turkiye social media ban for under-15s takes effect Nov 1
Article:
Turkiye social media ban for under-15s takes effect Nov 1
AFP
ISTANBUL: Turkiye on Saturday formally declared a ban on the use of social media for under-15s, scheduled to come into effect on November 1.
It has joined a growing number of countries legislating to protect children and teenagers from the harmful effects of online platforms.
The official state journal published the decision following the adoption of a law by parliament in April.
It stipulates that social media providers must "take the necessary technical and administrative measures, including age verification, to implement" protections for young people.
"No service likely to produce an addictive effect in children may be offered."
Countries including Australia have introduced restrictions on social media for children and others such as Britain and France are pushing to do the same.
They aim to protect children from digital risks such as screen addiction, lack of sleep, bullying and eating disorders.
Rights groups have complained of restrictions on freedom of expression in Turkey targeting LGBTQ communities, the media and the political opposition. Numerous social media accounts have been blocked in recent weeks.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tiger spotted roaming by roadside near Fraser's Hill
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Malayan tiger was spotted roaming along the road shoulder near Fraser's Hill heading towards Kuala Kubu Baru (KKB), Selangor.
The sighting was shared in a viral post on Threads by the account 'peann999', accompanied by two photos showing the wild animal standing at the roadside near the forest.
According to the post, the tiger was spotted near the GS Gap Chorocco trek area, about one kilometre from the Fraser's Hill junction heading towards KKB.
The user issued a warning to all road users and hikers using the route.
"Do not stop, do not open your windows. Do not get out of the car. The tiger was spotted roaming by the roadside," the post read.
Meanwhile, when contacted, the Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) said it is investigating the tiger's presence in the area.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: India detains 'cockroach' leaders ahead of election protest
Article:
NEW DELHI: Indian police detained the head of the satirical "cockroach" online movement on Saturday, the group said, ahead of a major protest against the Election Commission that triggered strict security measures.
The demonstration, due to take place in New Delhi, is the culmination of weeks of opposition mobilisation following allegations of misconduct during a nationwide voter-roll revision by the Election Commission of India (ECI).
Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke and two other leaders were detained before disembarking from a flight in the capital, the youth-led CJP said in a social media post, while television networks aired footage showing uniformed police aboard the plane.
"It's official... we are living under an absolute dictatorship," Arvind Kejriwal of the opposition Aam Aadmi Party said in a statement.
"Arresting cockroaches straight off their flight shows an unprecedented level of fear."
Opposition parties and other critics say the voter-roll revision could disenfranchise millions of voters and benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party.
The ECI has rejected allegations of impropriety, saying the "special intensive revision" was intended to remove duplicate and ineligible voters.
Delhi has been under a strict security clampdown since Friday, with tens of thousands of police and paramilitary personnel deployed to stop those seeking to reach the main protest site in the heart of the city.
Authorities have closed dozens of metro stations, cancelled several trains coming to Delhi and temporarily shut down mobile internet around the protest site.
AFP reporters saw police chasing down protesters on Saturday and hauling them into vehicles around central Delhi.
More than 200 protesters have been detained so far, local media reports said.
Media outlets, including the Scroll and Newslaundry, said their journalists had also been detained.
AFP was unable to reach police for comment on the reported detentions.
The protests are widely seen as a reprise of the "cockroach" movement's mass mobilisation in July, which led to the education minister stepping down over an examination scandal.
This time, they are demanding ECI chief Gyanesh Kumar resign from his post.
- 'Choking the city' -
The allegations are a fresh challenge for 76-year-old Modi during his third term in office.
Opposition parties have long alleged that legitimate voters are being struck off voter lists in India, the world's largest democracy with 1.4 billion people.
But the issue blew up last month when the Indian Express reported that key decisions linked to the revision were likely taken without the approval of two of the three election commissioners.
The ECI, a constitutional body, says all its decisions were unanimous and legally valid.
Sanjeev Takshak, one of a handful of protesters who managed to reach close to the protest site on Saturday, said he had come there out of "a sense of duty."
"The state is choking the entire city to prevent people from expressing their opinion," Takshak, a lawyer, said.
"It is absolutely not fair," the 42-year-old told AFP.
Delhi Police said they had taken the steps to ensure law and order.
"People should be able to raise their concerns peacefully," the force said in a statement. "Our responsibility is to create the conditions in which they can do that safely, while keeping the city functioning."
Amnesty International denounced the "lockdown-like restrictions."
"Peaceful protesters must be able to demand accountability from those in power without facing intimidation, arbitrary detention, or sweeping restrictions on their freedoms," it said in a statement.
The voter list overhaul, which began in 2025, has led to more than 133 million names being excluded from draft rolls.
The exclusions include duplicate entries and people found to have died.
The poll body said the exercise identifies fraudulently registered voters and aims to prevent "foreign illegal immigrants" from casting ballots.
Critics say the drive has disproportionately affected marginalised and minority communities.
Members of Modi's party have long alleged that large numbers of undocumented Muslim migrants from neighbouring Bangladesh have fraudulently entered India's electoral rolls.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia, Egypt ink four MoUs, strengthen bilateral cooperation
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia and Egypt signed four memoranda of understanding (MoU) today to strengthen bilateral cooperation in empowering women, higher education, tourism and investments.
The exchanges of all four MoUs were witnessed by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi.
The first MoU involved the empowerment of woman, between Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri and Egyptian Foreign Affairs, Emigration and Expatriates Minister Dr Badr Ahmed Mohamed Abdelatty.
The second, involving higher education, was between Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir and Abdelatty.
For tourism, the MoU was between Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing and Abdelatty.
The final MoU was between the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) and Egypt's General Authority for Investment and Free Zones.
The exchange of documents for this MoU was between Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and Egypt's Investment and Foreign Trade Minister Dr Mohamed Farid Saleh.
El-Sisi is in Malaysia for a two-day state visit on the invitation of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia.
He was earlier
accorded a state welcome
at Istana Negara.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Goat herder loses RM8,000 after flash flood kills 10 goats
Article:
GUA MUSANG: A 69-year-old man suffered losses of nearly RM8,000 after 10 of his goats died in a flash flood at Taman Kesedar Putra here today.
Mohamad Sapiin said this was the first such incident since he started rearing goats more than five years ago.
He said the area near the junction beneath a bridge in the housing estate was frequently inundated during heavy rain, but the water usually receded quickly and had never affected his goat pen.
"Water usually recedes within one to two hours and has never reached the goat pen, which is more than 100 metres away.
"However, heavy rain around midnight last night caused a nearby stream to overflow."
He said most of the dead goats had been ready for sale, including Boer goats worth up to RM2,000 each.
Following the incident, he sought assistance from the Civil Defence Force to move nine other goats to safety.
Meanwhile, Galas assemblyman Datuk Mohd Syahbuddin Hashim said he had contacted Gua Musang district officer Datuk Mohd Roshdi Ismail to request that the Gua Musang District Council convene a special meeting to address infrastructure problems in the area.
"As of noon today, the floodwaters had yet to recede," he said
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bar Council, TI-M urge audit and accountability in e-Jamin fallout
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government must insist on formal written contracts with service providers to ensure full accountability in protecting public interests after the e-Jamin online court bail system incident, the Malaysian Bar said today.
Its president, Anand Raj, said a formal contract setting out clear terms and minimum service standards under service level agreements (SLAs) is vital when public services are involved.
"This is to ensure that service providers can and are held accountable, and that the public, largely families who put up bail money, are protected by the government acting in its best interests," he told the
New Straits Times
.
Anand was responding to the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) findings that the e-Jamin online court bail system operated for five years
without a formal contract
with the federal government.
PAC chairman Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin had said the system, which has been operating at 192 courts nationwide since Jan 10, 2020, had no letter of appointment, letter of acceptance, letter of intent, or formal contract with the government throughout that period.
On Thursday, Dapat Vista (DV), which operates the e-Jamin online court bail system, had offered three options to the government to formalise its operations.
The company said it submitted the proposals to the Finance Ministry via the Office of the Chief Registrar of the Federal Court on Aug 18 last year.
"The options include a direct buyout of the system by the government, a subscription service model, or a five-year hybrid operating model before a full takeover," DV said in a statement.
The system was launched in January 2020 to enhance and simplify court bail payments.
Anand said safeguarding bail funds must remain the government's top priority.
"The priority should always be for the government to act in a manner that safeguards and properly accounts for bail monies, avoids delays in refunds, and protects and preserves the administration of criminal justice and the rights and liberties of accused persons," he said.
He said the PAC's revelations went well beyond financial discrepancies, exposing serious governance gaps in public service delivery and raising critical questions about how sureties' bail deposits are handled.
"The Bar was not previously aware of the absence of contract documentation between the government and the e-Jamin service provider and is surprised by this revelation by the PAC," he said.
He said, according to the PAC report, the prolonged absence of a formal contract appeared to stem from advice by the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) that such documentation was unnecessary.
"It is unclear why that view was taken and why this state of affairs remained unchanged for so many years."
Transparency International Malaysia (TI-M) president Raymon Ram said government action on the e-Jamin online court bail system must extend beyond simply formalising a contract after the fact.
He said the government must immediately safeguard bail monies, fully account for past lapses, and implement structural reforms to prevent similar governance failures in the future.
"The government must first establish and publicly confirm the location, status, and reconciliation of all active e-Jamin bail funds. Public money must be held in a legally compliant structure, properly segregated, and protected from private operator risks.
"Second, an independent forensic audit and full reconciliation should cover the entire period of e-Jamin's operation.
"This should trace all bail transactions, the RM193.71 million active balance reported as of Dec 31, 2024, the RM130.8 million invested, all investment returns generated, and the RM557,258 reconciliation discrepancy."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia, Egypt to hold Joint Commission meeting in Q1 next year
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and Egypt will hold a Joint Commission meeting in the first quarter of next year to strengthen bilateral cooperation, particularly in trade, investment and transportation.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the two countries' foreign ministers had agreed to the meeting.
"Whilst we have achieved a phenomenal increase this year, rising to 74.7 per cent of trade, but that is from a very, very low base.
"Therefore, collaboration with Egypt will give Malaysia immense opportunities to expand trade, investment, tourism and cooperation across various sectors," he said at a joint press conference with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi.
El-Sisi is in Malaysia for his first state visit to the country since assuming office in June 2014. The visit is at the invitation of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia.
Anwar said other potential areas of bilateral cooperation included semiconductors, electrical and electronics (E&E), agriculture and pharmaceuticals.
"We have been trying to source pharmaceutical products from emerging economies and BRICS countries, and I think Egypt has the potential to be one destination that we solicit pharmaceutical products from."
Education was another important area of cooperation, with opportunities extending beyond Islamic studies to engineering, medicine, E&E, digital technology and artificial intelligence (AI), he said.
"I have told President El-Sisi that education in Egypt is not limited to Al-Azhar University, which remains important for Islamic education. Egypt has also expanded its capabilities in E&E, digital technology, AI, engineering and medicine.
"Many of our doctors received their training in Egypt. I do not want to create the impression that only Islamic studies are important. While they remain significant, educational cooperation should also encompass other fields of study," he said.
Anwar added that both countries should strengthen cooperation in defence procurement and joint training.
"Although our countries are geographically distant, our hearts are close," he said.
Anwar said his meeting with El-Sisi also covered international issues, including the unresolved situation in the Strait of Hormuz and its implications for Iran.
"We have taken a strong position against the atrocities inflicted upon the people of Palestine and Gaza, as well as the intransigence and violence perpetrated by Israel."
He said Egypt had provided substantial assistance to Malaysia in its efforts to deliver humanitarian aid to the Palestinians, although Malaysia's contribution was modest compared with Egypt's.
"You have provided tremendous help and assistance to the Palestinians. Malaysia has also contributed, albeit on a smaller scale, through you and your office personally.
"When we brought injured Palestinians from Gaza to Malaysia, we coordinated through your office and your military intelligence."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Elderly man injured after crane overturns onto care home roof in Penang
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM: An 84-year-old man was injured when a crane overturned and crashed onto the roof of an elderly care home in Permatang Tinggi today.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said the department received an emergency call at 12.38pm.
He said the crane was believed to have lost stability while parked on uneven ground before overturning and striking the roof of the dormitory housing residents.
"The victim sustained a head injury and was taken to hospital by Health Ministry personnel before firefighters arrived," he said.
John said a total of 49 people, comprising residents and workers, were at the premises when the incident occurred.
They included 20 men, one of whom was injured, 17 women and 11 workers, including the crane driver.
The remaining occupants were unharmed.
Firefighters monitored the affected area to ensure safety and cordoned off the scene to control public movement and prevent unauthorised entry.
The operation was brought under control at 1.15pm and concluded at 1.45pm, involving police and Health Ministry personnel.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thunderstorm warning issued for all states until 6pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning, with heavy rain and strong winds expected across all states until 6pm today.
In a statement today, MetMalaysia said the warning covers the whole of Perlis, Terengganu, Negri Sembilan, Melaka, and the Federal Territories.
In Kedah, affected areas include Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Padang Terap, Sik, and Baling.
In Penang, the warning applies to Northeast (Timor Laut) and Southwest (Barat Daya) districts.
For Perak, affected areas include Larut, Matang and Selama, Kerian, Manjung, Bagan Datuk, Perak Tengah, Hilir Perak, and Hulu Perak.
In Kelantan, affected areas cover Kuala Krai and Jeli, while in Pahang, the warning involves Rompin and Jerantut.
In Selangor, the warning covers Sabak Bernam, Hulu Selangor, Gombak, Kuala Selangor, Klang, Petaling, and Hulu Langat, while in Sarawak, the warning covers Sri Aman (Lubok Antu).
In Sabah, affected areas include Tawau (Tawau, Semporna, Kunak, and Lahad Datu), Sandakan (Kinabatangan, Sandakan, Telupid, Labuk and Sugut, and Paitan), West Coast (Kota Belud and Ranau), and Kudat (Kota Marudu).
Thunderstorm warnings are short-term alerts issued when there are signs of thunderstorms with rain intensity exceeding 20mm per hour that are occurring or expected to last for more than an hour. The warning is valid for up to six hours.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police take over probes into bullying, teacher assault cases in Perak
Article:
IPOH: School authorities have completed administrative procedures, including discussions with the victims' families, following separate bullying and alleged teacher assault cases in Chemor and Pengkalan Hulu.
Perak Education, Higher Education, Youth and Sports Committee chairman Datuk Khairudin Abu Hanipah said investigations into both cases had been handed over to the police after the victims lodged reports.
Khairudin said the district education offices (PPD) and state Education Department had completed their administrative processes.
"This involved consensus meetings between the PPD, the schools and the victims' families to find the best win-win solution.
"The Education Ministry's 1-3-7 reporting procedure was followed to ensure harmony in schools is maintained," he said.
He urged all parties to allow the police to complete their investigations, adding that certain details only became clear after police reports were lodged.
"For example, in the Chemor case, the police report was only lodged in October, although the incident occurred in July," he said.
He was speaking to reporters after representing the Perak Menteri Besar at the state-level National Sports Day celebration at the Perak Youth and Sports Complex today.
Khairudin said he could not comment further as police investigations were ongoing.
On Oct 5, it was
reported
that single mother Noor Azwani Ahamad, 43, claimed her two sons had been bullied and subjected to violence involving students and a teacher at a school in Chemor.
In a separate incident in Pengkalan Hulu on Sept 23, an 11-year-old boy claimed a teacher had hit him on the head.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Customs integrity crucial to preventing cargo fraud, former prosecutor says
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Strong enforcement and integrity among customs officers are essential to preventing cargo fraud, as legislation alone cannot stop shipments from being unlawfully diverted, a former deputy public prosecutor says.
Devanandan Subramaniam, who previously served as a commercial crime deputy public prosecutor at the Attorney-General's Chambers, said weaknesses in customs procedures could allow cargo to be discharged even when essential ownership documents are missing.
"You can have all the legislation in place, no integrity, things can still go past," he said at a forum titled "Strengthening Malaysia's Downstream Petroleum Value Chain and Identifying Gaps and Enabling Factors Within Malaysia Regulatory Landscape".
Devanandan was asked to explain the challenges of prosecuting cargo fraud cases, including the distinction between suspicious transactions and criminal offences, the process from investigation to prosecution, and the parties who could ultimately be charged.
He was also asked to share his experience handling such cases and advise the shipping industry on compliance measures to prevent cargo fraud.
Drawing from a case he prosecuted more than 20 years ago, Devanandan recounted how cargo worth about US$2 million, originally destined for Chittagong, Bangladesh, was diverted to Port Klang.
He said the shipment originated from Belawan, Sumatra, but the charterer subsequently instructed the vessel's master to discharge the cargo in Port Klang instead.
The consignor, however, retained the original bills of lading, which served as evidence of title to the goods.
Despite this, the cargo was discharged after the clearance agent obtained the necessary approvals.
Devanandan said investigations uncovered forged documents, including K1 forms, prompting the prosecution of the company's managing director for using a forged document as genuine and the company for receiving stolen property.
However, the case was eventually thrown out after the prosecution failed to establish that the managing director knew, or had reasonable grounds to know, that the documents were forged.
He said prosecuting such cases was challenging because proving that a document was fraudulent did not necessarily establish the accused person's knowledge of the forgery.
Devanandan stressed that customs officers played a critical role in ensuring that cargo documentation was properly verified before goods were released.
"They play the most important role. As long as they ensure that everything is in order, such things will not happen," he said.
While acknowledging that cargo documentation processes had evolved towards electronic transmission since the case he handled, Devanandan said enforcement and integrity remained essential safeguards.
He added that procedural requirements would be ineffective if officers failed to ensure compliance at the point of clearance.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Khazanah: 2027 Budget to boost competitiveness, ease cost of living
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The 2027 Budget will continue to strengthen Malaysia's long-term competitiveness and economic growth while prioritising the people through measures to ease the cost of living, raise wages and widen opportunities, Khazanah Nasional Bhd said.
Its managing director, Datuk Amirul Feisal Wan Zahir, said the budget came at a crucial time as Malaysia navigated a volatile global environment marked by geopolitical uncertainty, supply chain pressures and elevated fuel prices amid the ongoing conflict in West Asia.
He said 2027 Budget emphasised quality growth, with a focus on strategic sectors such as semiconductors, the energy transition, infrastructure, enterprise development and talent to build a stronger, more competitive and future-ready economy.
"These priorities are critical to deepening Malaysia's industrial base, enhancing economic complexity and creating higher-value opportunities for businesses and workers," he said in a statement.
Amirul Feisal said the budget also maintained an inclusive approach to ensure national development benefited all segments of society, including workers, youth, entrepreneurs, Bumiputera companies, micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), and communities facing economic and climate-related challenges.
He added that the budget's focus on vendor development, innovation and access to new markets would create further opportunities for Bumiputera businesses to expand.
Khazanah will continue to support the government's economic and development priorities through initiatives such as Dana Impak, Jelawang Capital, Dana Ciptawan, Dana Warisan, K-Youth, Bakat Madani and Yayasan Hasanah, which support enterprise development, talent, innovation, community resilience and long-term national competitiveness.
"We will continue to collaborate with other government-linked investment companies under the Finance Ministry's GEAR-uP programme to mobilise capital more effectively through disciplined investments, catalytic partnerships and impact-driven programmes that help build a more resilient Malaysia for current and future generations," he added.
On Friday, Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim tabled Budget 2027, amounting to RM459.8 billion, comprising RM376.8 billion in federal operating expenditure and RM83 billion in federal development expenditure.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: From 'waad' to 'zeitgeist', Anwar highlights words in 2027 Budget speech
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has shared the meanings of selected words used in his 2027 Budget speech, shedding light on terms that convey ideas about governance, heritage and intergenerational responsibility.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, shared the definitions in a Facebook post today, inviting the public to learn the meanings behind the words.
"Let's learn with Guru," he wrote.
Among the words he highlighted were waad, meaning a promise or pledge; lighad, meaning tomorrow or the future; and seyogia, meaning what should or ought to be done.
Other terms included beranotasi, referring to additional explanatory notes; menata, meaning to arrange or organise systematically; and inayat, referring to help or divine grace.
Pranata refers to a system or set of rules governing social life, while filasuf means philosophers.
Anwar also highlighted Ithaca, an ancient Greek island known in literature as the homeland of Odysseus. It is often associated with memories of home, history and an enduring sense of belonging.
Other words included dasawarsa, meaning a period of 10 years or a decade; khulasah, meaning a summary or the essence of an issue; and turath, referring to inherited intellectual and scholarly traditions, particularly in Islamic thought.
Anwar also highlighted the expression zaman mansang, linking it to the German term Zeitgeist, which describes the spirit, defining characteristics and demands of a particular era.
The expression carries a deeper sense of the responsibilities and obligations imposed by the times, including the need for the present generation to act responsibly towards those who come after them, a concept known as intergenerational responsibility.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Expert calls for tighter surveillance of ship-to-ship oil transfers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia must strengthen maritime surveillance and enforcement to detect suspicious ship-to-ship (STS) oil transfers amid allegations that its waters are being used to facilitate the movement of sanctioned Iranian oil, an academic says.
Maritime industry and logistics expert Prof Nazery Khalid said authorities should step up patrols and use satellite technology and intelligence-sharing to identify suspicious vessel movements.
"The Coast Guard and Maritime Division should conduct patrols to keep an eye on ships behaving suspiciously," he said at a forum titled "Strengthening Malaysia's Downstream Petroleum Value Chain and Identifying Gaps and Enabling Factors Within Malaysia Regulatory Landscape.
The forum was organised by Maritime Network, together with Universiti Malaysia Terengganu (UMT).
Nazery said STS transfers were legitimate and highly regulated maritime operations, but must comply with national rules and international safety and environmental standards.
He said satellite monitoring could help authorities identify vessels remaining close to one another for extended periods, while specialised service providers could assist enforcement agencies in detecting suspicious activities.
"We need to ensure that ship-to-ship transfer is done in accordance with national rules, in designated areas, and ensuring that it adheres to high safety and environmental standards," he said.
Another panellist, Orkim chief executive officer Captain Cheah Sin Bi, said vessels with suspicious histories and operating practices could provide warning signs of potentially illicit transfers.
He cited vessels that had changed names repeatedly, switched registrations between countries and switched off equipment during transfers.
"The name has changed like 15 times. The registry has changed about five different countries, and then the equipment has been switched off during the transfer, so you think that something is not right," he said.
Cheah said shipping operators should conduct proper know-your-customer checks, scrutinise contractual arrangements and consult their Protection and Indemnity clubs when uncertain about a transaction.
He also urged operators to question unusually lucrative offers that deviated from prevailing market rates.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mother mourns daughter who dreamed of bringing family under one roof
Article:
BATU PAHAT: A sombre mood enveloped Sultanah Nora Ismail Hospital's Forensic Department here today as Hairul Aziah Rahmad arrived to claim the body of her daughter, who died in a fiery crash yesterday.
Overcome with grief, the 52-year-old woman had to be supported by family members as she repeatedly expressed her wish to see her daughter's face for the last time.
She said she had arrived too late at the accident scene at Batu 1, Jalan Yong Peng-Ayer Hitam, yesterday.
"When I arrived at the scene, all that was left of the car was its frame," she said when met at the hospital.
Her daughter, Siti Nurmaisarah Abd Jalil, 22, and her cousin, Siti Nur Batrisya Mohd Khalid, 22,
died when their car
caught fire following a collision with a lorry.
Hairul Aziah's sister-in-law, Zahrah Suliman, 61, said Siti Nurmaisarah had helped support the family since her parents separated, as her mother's health condition limited her ability to work.
"She was a good daughter and worked hard to support the family. She had planned to live with her family in a new house after getting married.
"She had told us that she wanted to bring us to live with her. She did so much to help the family, including taking care of her brother.
"But sadly, her dreams were not realised.
"That is what makes our family so heartbroken," she said.
Zahrah said she was looking for a new house so that Hairul Aziah and her brother, who is a person with disabilities, could live with her.
Siti Nurmaisarah had hoped to bring the family together under one roof after her marriage, but those hopes were cut short by the tragedy.
Meanwhile, Siti Nur Batrisya's mother, Hamidah Sulaiman, said her youngest child, who was affectionately known as 'adik', and Siti Nurmaisarah had been inseparable since childhood.
"Both of them loved cats and would feed those they came across. Sometimes, they would even bring the cats home," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Eight-metre-deep sinkhole forces closure of Gua Musang-Kota Baru road
Article:
GUA MUSANG: An eight-metre-deep sinkhole at FT08 Jalan Gua Musang - Kota Baru near here forced the complete closure of the road to all vehicles today.
The Public Works Department said in a statement that the incident occurred at 9.05am near the Kesedar Recreation Park.
Following the closure, all motorists are advised to use the alternative route via Jalan Pulai to Bandar Baru Gua Musang.
District police chief Superintendent Sik Choon Foo confirmed the incident and advised road users to exercise caution and adhere to instructions issued by authorities.
Galas assemblyman Datuk Mohd Syahbuddin Hashim said immediate repair work is necessary as the affected road serves as a primary route for residents, particularly those living in Taman Kesedar Putra and Taman Kesedar Jaya.
"Immediate repairs are needed as this is the main route for residents commuting and sending their children to school. There are also concerns that the sinkhole could expand to the adjacent road," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Families of missing Malaysians accept painful change to death declaration period
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Though painful, families of missing Malaysians are prepared to accept Nepal's proposal to shorten the period for declaring missing disaster victims dead.
Sivakumar Kalimuthu, 63, acknowledged he had to accept the proposal by the Nepali government to shorten the declaration period to 45 days from 12 years.
Sivakumar, whose wife, Kalai Mathe Karuppaiah, 57, is missing, said the Malaysian government has not issued any official notification regarding the proposal so far.
"We have to accept it because the incident has already happened and we have no direct line of communication with them to voice feedback to the Nepali government.
"We were previously told that death certificates are usually issued after seven years if victims remain missing, though in this case, the period was shortened to three years.
"Nepal's decision on the proposal may make it easier for us to transfer the victim's assets to other family members," he said when contacted today.
Sharing a similar sentiment, Hani Othman, wife of Senior Fire Officer II Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa, admitted it was difficult to accept the decision since no alternatives were provided to next of kin.
"I have mixed feelings about accepting any decision regarding Nepal's proposal.
"However, as next of kin, we have to accept whatever the government decides.
"I only learned about this through social media and am still unsure of the exact decision regarding the proposal," she said.
Meanwhile, efforts to obtain a response from the Malaysian government regarding the proposal remain ongoing, with the Foreign Ministry reportedly reviewing the recommendation.
Yesterday, Nepal reportedly proposed shortening the current 12-year missing period for declaring victims dead to 45 days.
Kathmandu proposed this following devastating floods in Nepal that claimed numerous lives from various nations.
Nepal was struck on Aug 26 by a disaster described as a Himalayan Tsunami following rockfalls and snow avalanches, which killed more than 1,400 people and left over 6,000 untraceable.
Search, rescue, and recovery operations remain underway in several flood-affected areas following widespread destruction that left over 70,000 residents directly affected and displaced.
During the floods, settlements on high-altitude slopes near the Tibet border were severely impacted by swift floodwaters following a sudden glacial lake outburst.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fahmi: RM150m Postal Fund to begin operations in first quarter of 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government has set aside RM150 million for the Postal Fund, which is scheduled to begin operations in the first quarter of 2027.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the fund aims to guarantee the smooth implementation of the Universal Service Obligation (USO), which is crucial for mail delivery services in rural areas, remote regions, and islands.
"With rapid technological changes, the expansion of the digital economy and the growth of e-commerce necessitate adjustments to policy, legislation, and operations.
"The government's focus is ensuring that postal and courier sector workers are well protected, their welfare safeguards maintained, and that they receive fair compensation and wages," he said after officiating World Post Day.
Fahmi said the Postal Fund will be managed by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and will operate on a framework similar to the Universal Service Provision (USP) fund in the telecommunications sector.
"Although the fund has been provided for under the Postal Services Act since 2012, no previous administration had taken steps to start it until now," he added.
Fahmi said MCMC will issue a full statement detailing the fund's expanded scope, which will go beyond basic postal services to cover goods deliveries to remote areas outside urban centres.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sultan Ibrahim confers Darjah Utama Seri Negara award on Egyptian President El-Sisi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, today consented to confer the Darjah Utama Seri Mahkota Negara (DMN) award on Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, who is currently in Malaysia on a two-day state visit.
El-Sisi was conferred the award at Istana Negara in a special ceremony at Dewan Seri Maharaja prior to a state banquet hosted in honour of the Egyptian leader, who arrived in the country yesterday.
Also at the ceremony were Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, Investment, Trade, and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, dignitaries, and an Egyptian delegation.
Earlier, El-Sisi was accorded a state welcoming ceremony at the Istana Negara parade square upon his arrival at 10.08am.
El-Sisi's visit, at the invitation of Sultan Ibrahim, is the first by an Egyptian president to Malaysia in nearly three decades. The last visit, by former President Mohamed Hosni Mubarak, took place in November 1997 for the G-15 Summit in Kuala Lumpur. Mubarak also paid an official visit as Egyptian Vice President in 1979.
Malaysia and Egypt established diplomatic relations in 1959.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Soldier charged after pistol, ammunition found at Sungai Besi army camp
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A soldier arrested with a pistol and dozens of rounds of ammunition at an army camp in Sungai Besi on Sept 29 was charged at the Jalan Duta Courts on Thursday.
Cheras district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Rosdi Daud said the suspect was charged after investigation papers were submitted to the deputy public prosecutor (DPP).
"The suspect was charged at the Jalan Duta Courts, Kuala Lumpur, on Oct 8.
"The investigation papers were submitted to the DPP, who approved charges against the suspect under Section 8 of the Firearms (Increased Penalties) Act 1971 and Section 8(a) of the Arms Act 1960," he said in a statement today.
Rosdi said investigations are ongoing to identify the owner and source of the seized pistol and ammunition.
On Oct 3, it was reported that the soldier was
arrested
in a parking area inside the camp on Sept 29, with a pistol, dozens of rounds of ammunition, and liquid suspected to be ketum.
The suspect, in his 30s, has three prior criminal offences involving two drug-related cases and one other criminal case.
He was remanded for five days, with the remand period extended by another five days until Oct 8 to assist in investigations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Grieving mother haunted by memories of her three children killed in Pontian accident
Article:
PONTIAN, Oct 10 — The mother of the three siblings who tragically died in an accident at Kampung Parit Haji Siraj, Kayu Ara Pasong here, admits that she still finds it difficult to look at her children’s clothes and school bags as they serve as painful reminders of them.
Julaiha Munaji, 44, said the simultaneous loss of Nor Daniel Aiman Norlizan, 18, Nor Daniel Fikri Norlizan, 11, and Puteri Naufa Raisha Norlizan, 8, is the heaviest trial she and her family have ever faced.
She shared that the loss of her youngest child, Puteri Naufa, is felt the most because the only daughter among her six children was exceptionally close to her.
“I have six children, five boys and one girl. For years, my husband and I prayed for a daughter, but I was only blessed to have her with me for eight years.
“Even though I lost her two days ago, I accept it with a quiet heart and am grateful for the chance to raise her, even if it was only for a short time,” she told Bernama when met at her home in Kampung Parit Haji Siraj today.
Julaiha said among the things she misses the most is her daily routine of preparing breakfast and packed meals for her children before starting the day.
She added that she can still vividly picture the playful antics of her three children in the yard every evening, memories that are hard to forget.
“It will probably take time for me to get used to this loss. Losing even one child is heavy enough, but losing three all at once is unbearable,” she said.
Last Thursday, the three siblings died after the motorcycle they were riding collided with a lorry on Jalan Parit Haji Sirat, Kayu Ara Pasong at around 7:20 am, just after returning from Sekolah Kebangsaan Parit Sapran.
At the time, Nor Daniel Aiman was on his way back after taking his two younger siblings to the school to inform them that classes were canceled due to deteriorating air quality caused by haze.
Pontian District Police Chief Supt Hadzrat Hussein Moin Hussain reported that two of the pillion riders died at the scene, while the motorcycle rider passed away while on the way to Pontian Hospital.
All schools in Johor were closed last Thursday and Friday due to the declining air quality, affecting more than 1,000 schools and approximately 600,000 students. — Bernama

Title: DPM Zahid wants tahfiz graduates equipped for careers in technology, engineering and medicine
Article:
BANGI, Oct 10 — Tahfiz graduates should have wider opportunities to pursue higher education and professional careers in fields such as technology, engineering and medicine to meet the country’s evolving workforce needs, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said.
He said tahfiz education should go beyond Quran memorisation by equipping graduates with the knowledge, skills and qualifications needed to pursue a broader range of careers.
“My principle is simple. Tahfiz graduates should not have to choose between religion and their ambitions. They should be given the opportunity to deepen their religious knowledge while acquiring the skills and qualifications needed for professional careers,” he said at the 10th Huffaz Nusantara Permata Al-Quran Convocation at the German-Malaysian Institute here today.
Ahmad Zahid, who chairs the National Tahfiz Council, said advances in artificial intelligence (AI), the digital economy and high technology made it increasingly important for tahfiz graduates to develop skills that would enable them to compete across various sectors.
As such, he said tahfiz education must also keep pace with the country’s human capital needs by providing more pathways to universities, technical and vocational education and training (TVET) institutions, industry and professional fields.
Achieving this would require cooperation among the government, tahfiz institutions, universities and industry to ensure graduates had clear opportunities to progress after completing their studies.
“Tahfiz graduates must not be left to find their own way after graduation. The ecosystem must help them move on to the next stage,” he said.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, said efforts to strengthen tahfiz education included enhancing the National Tahfiz Education Policy, developing the Malaysian Tahfiz Recognition Standard and strengthening pathways through the Malaysian Tahfiz Certificate to broaden graduates’ education and career options.
He also welcomed the increased allocation for Islamic affairs, pondok schools, tahfiz institutions and people’s religious schools under Budget 2027, as well as improved allowances for religious teachers and mosque personnel
“This reflects the government’s commitment to supporting those involved in Islamic religious affairs, and is a positive development that deserves the support of all parties,” he said.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, when tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday, announced that the allocation for Islamic affairs had been increased to RM3.1 billion from RM2.6 billion this year. — Bernama

Title: Lights on: Works Department to extend streetlight operating hours during haze
Article:
PONTIAN, Oct 10 — The Public Works Department (JKR) will extend the operating hours of its streetlights by up to two hours during haze conditions to help improve visibility for road users.
Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan said the measure, implemented through JKR’s Electrical Engineering Branch, was prompted by haze conditions that had reduced visibility and increased the risk of accidents.
He said streetlights using timer systems currently typically operated from 7 pm to 7 am.
“Each streetlight has a timer setting that can be adjusted. During haze conditions, the operating hours can be extended by up to two hours.
“We will also refer the matter to local authorities, such as municipal councils and city halls, to encourage them to take similar measures,” he told reporters after visiting the family of three siblings who died in an accident at Kampung Parit Haji Siraj here today.
The three siblings, aged eight to 18, were killed on Thursday after the motorcycle they were on collided with a lorry on Jalan Parit Haji Sirat in Kayu Ara Pason amid hazy weather and limited visibility.
Ahmad also advised road users to exercise greater caution and ensure safe visibility when driving in hazy conditions. — Bernama

Title: Air quality acceptable for now, Kedah schools to open as usual tomorrow
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Oct 10 — All educational institutions in Kedah will operate as usual tomorrow as the Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at all monitoring areas in the state were recorded below 100 as of 2 pm today.
The Kedah State Education Department (JPN) said in a statement that this was, however, subject to any further directives from the Ministry of Education and the relevant authorities.
“The Kedah JPN expresses its appreciation for the concern and decree of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, regarding the importance of safeguarding the safety, health and welfare of students and education personnel following the haze affecting several areas in the country.
“The API readings are below 100, so all educational institutions in Kedah will operate as usual,” the statement said.
The Kedah JPN said school administrators and educational institutions had nevertheless been reminded to remain alert to the latest developments, monitor API readings through official Department of Environment channels and take appropriate measures to ensure the safety and health of students and education personnel.
“Schools should also pay close attention to students and education personnel experiencing health problems, particularly those who are sensitive to air quality conditions, and take appropriate action if any students or education personnel show signs of ill health.
“The Kedah JPN will continue to monitor developments in the haze situation and coordinate action with all District Education Offices and educational institutions based on the latest readings and directives from the authorities,” it said. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi urges Malaysians to prioritise mental health in World Mental Health Day post
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 —The public should prioritise their mental health and not hesitate to seek help when experiencing stress or feeling overburdened by the demands of daily life, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said.
He said mental health should be cared for alongside physical health, particularly when dealing with the demands of work, family and everyday life.
“In the midst of busy work, family and daily life, do not forget to look after our mental health just as we look after our physical health,” he said in a Facebook post in conjunction with World Mental Health Day today.
Fahmi said those who felt overwhelmed, exhausted or struggled to cope on their own should talk to someone they trusted and seek help if necessary.
He also reminded the public that taking a break and giving themselves some space was nothing to feel guilty about.
World Mental Health Day is observed on October 10 every year to raise public awareness of the importance of mental health worldwide. — Bernama
